messages:
maria: kicking off a permissions sweep in staging this morning — focusing on service accounts with owner/editor roles and any KMS bindings. will run in canary mode against two namespaces (staging-a, staging-b).

devon: sounds good. do we have the runbook and a non-prod rollback plan? also want to avoid colliding with the nightly deploy.

natalie: added runbook link https://redwood.internal/runbooks/perm-sweep-staging and a checklist. rollback steps are under section 3. small note: avoid 03:00–05:00 window.

irfan: heads up — some legacy svcaccts surfaced during last scan had project-level KMS grants. those are the risky ones (customer-key access). manual review required for any project-level binding.

maria: exactly. plan: auto-detect + create tickets for manual remediation on KMS-grant hits. running a quick detection query locally:
```bash
# list service accounts with owner/editor
gcloud projects get-iam-policy redwood-staging --format=json \| jq '.bindings[] | select(.role=="roles/owner" or .role=="roles/editor")'
```
please don't run this on prod.

sec-bot: [alert] policy-change detected: svcAcct:legacy-deployer@redwood-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com was granted roles/owner on project redwood-staging at 2026-03-20T09:12:04Z. ticket created: SEC-7123.

devon: I'll own the canary prune in staging-a at 10:15 — will remove owner from svcacct-test-canary and monitor. @sre-oncall can you watch metrics + flow logs for 15m post-change?

sre-oncall: on it. I'll tail the audit logs and watch for Decrypt/Encrypt errors and failed job traces. will alert on any elevated error rate.

natalie: suggested KMS audit filter to watch during canary:
```
resource.type="k8s_container" AND protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"
```
also check for long tail errors from workflows that touch crypto.

maria: quick scan results before canary: found 12 service accounts with owner/editor roles, 3 of those have KMS grants at project level. creating tickets SWEEP-121, SWEEP-122, SWEEP-123 and assigning to respective owners.

irfan: for the KMS hits, recommendation is to move bindings to key-level IAM and use least-priv roles. e.g., prefer roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on a key resource rather than project-level binding. note this in tickets.

devon: will include recommended gcloud to repair in the ticket, e.g.:
```bash
# remove project-level grant
gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding redwood-staging --member="serviceAccount:legacy-deployer@..." --role="roles/owner"
# add key-level binding
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding my-key --location=global --keyring=my-ring --member="serviceAccount:legacy-deployer@..." --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
```

maria: running the canary now in staging-a. output (truncated):
```
2026-03-20T10:15:03Z removed roles/owner from svcacct-test-canary
2026-03-20T10:15:18Z no failed decrypts detected in workflows (0 -> 0)
2026-03-20T10:20:00Z job-processor-1 reported transient timeout, retried successfully
```

sre-oncall: saw a single transient timeout that recovered. no crypto errors. rolling to staging-b tomorrow morning.

natalie: heads-up for ticket owners: annotate PRs with evidence (audit log snippets) and expected rollback steps. retention policy requires we keep remediation evidence in the ticket.

irfan: one more thing — watch for service accounts used by external integrations. if the SA is referenced from terraform state, coordinate with infra to update state or leave a temporary alias.

maria: noted. next steps: roll to staging-b tomorrow, then schedule a controlled prod window (post-approval). weekly sweep cadence proposed. anyone opposed?

devon: +1. prefer weekly for staging, monthly for prod.

sre-oncall: +1, will add a monitor to alert on any sudden spike in KMS decrypt failures after changes.

maria: thanks all :thumbsup: leaving notes in runbook and closing this thread. will post summary after staging-b run.
